newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Jan 30.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Jan 30.

text.p: Two of Mexico's main crude ports remained shut Thursday for the third consecutive day and a total of four Gulf of Mexico ports reported closed, the Communications and Transport Ministry said in its 1000 local/1600 GMT daily report.
Crude ports Pajaritos in Veracruz state and Dos Bocas in Tabasco state were shut on 1200 local/1800 GMT Tuesday as a cold front in the region brought fierce winds and high waves.
Further south along the gulf, the ports of Ciudad del Carmen and Campeche in Campeche state were shut amid winds of up to 30 km per hour.
Alvarado, Frontera, Salina Cruz and Puerto Madero were shut to smaller tourist and fishing ships.
The Gulf of Mexico cold front has weakened and should pass over the southeast of the country later in the day, the ministry bulletin said.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Gulf of Mexico, Caribbean and Pacific Coast.

Sunny with slight possibility of some rains. Colder temperatures along the Baja California peninsula and in the Gulf of Tehuantepec. Winds in the gulf at 20 to 25 knots (38 to 47 km/22 to 28 miles per hour) and waves eight to 10 feet high.

Weak cold front along northeast Gulf of Mexico extending toward the northern Yucatan peninsula. Lower temperatures and clouds with chance of light rain along the coasts of Tabasco and Campeche states and the Yucatan peninsula.
Winds in the region from the north and northeast at 15 to 20 knots (28 to 38 km/17 to 22 miles per hour).

Cold front and diverse clouds with isolated light rains along coast of Quintana Roo and central America. Winds from the northeast at 10 to 20 knots (19 to 38 km/11 to 22 miles per hour), with waves from five to seven feet high.
